analysis.title: Energy Futures: When Managed Money Brent Oil Selling Tops $6bn
key_insights: Managed Money Brent selling topped $6bn notional for only the 7th time in 5 years per CFTC Commitment of Traders. Managed Money sold $6.6bn from Oct 27 to Nov 3 alongside a 5.3% price drop. Liquidation ($4.9bn) was the main driver.

The selling followed signals that the US and Iran were more willing to reach a diplomatic solution. The period included reports that President Trump chose negotiations over strikes and that Supreme Leader Khamenei granted the Iranian President authority for dialogue.

Recent history points to continued weak flows. Since Liberation Day there were 3 similar instances of heavy Managed Money Brent selling, and each time negative activity persisted for the following 2 weeks, most notably after the initial Iran-US MOU in June 2026.

A longer lookback shows one swift reversal. Over May 28 to June 4, 2024, Managed Money sold $7.9bn on OPEC's scheduled end of voluntary output curbs. After OPEC ministers pushed back against the market reaction, Managed Money net length was fully restored.

The midterm elections added long terminations. On Nov 4 the Democratic sweep raised expectations of constraints on President Trump's agenda, including funding for overseas military operations. Brent fell 8.7% and open interest shed $2.7bn.
Per GS Futures Strategists' CTA framework, short-term momentum turned negative on Nov 4 for the first time since August, which unlocked additional selling.

Price stabilized afterward. Brent recouped 3.9% over Nov 5 and 6. Three-month implied volatility richened, normalized 25 delta put-call skew cheapened, and calls were repurchased, which GS reads as some bullish posturing in the option surface.

sector_views.rationale: Flows are expected to stay challenged on recent precedent, but the option surface showed bullish posturing after the Nov 4 drop.

risk_factors: Further Managed Money liquidation, as heavy selling has persisted for 2 weeks in each of the 3 instances since Liberation Day
Negative CTA momentum triggering additional systematic selling
Political constraints on US foreign policy and military funding after the Democratic midterm sweep
